Verified milestone code

These snippets are loaded from the downloadable solution that was built, migrated and tested locally. Type them rather than merely reading them. Lesson snippets isolate one idea and sometimes show an earlier, smaller Order shape; this checkpoint is the canonical cumulative version after refactoring, so do not paste every sketch into the final solution.

tutorial-snapshots/01-console/Program.cs
string customer = "Sarah";
int quantity = 3;
decimal unitPrice = 25m;
bool isPaid = true;

decimal total = CalculateTotal(quantity, unitPrice);
string size = ClassifyOrder(total);
bool hasValidQuantity = quantity > 0;
bool canFulfil = isPaid && total >= 50m;

if (total >= 100m)
{
    Console.WriteLine("Large order");
}
else
{
    Console.WriteLine("Small order");
}

int[] quantities = [quantity, 2, 1];
int totalQuantity = 0;
foreach (int itemQuantity in quantities)
{
    totalQuantity += itemQuantity;
}

decimal[] sampleTotals = [total, 100m, 55m, 220m, 10m];
foreach (decimal orderTotal in sampleTotals)
{
    if (orderTotal >= 100m)
        Console.WriteLine($"Qualifying total: {orderTotal:C}");
}

Console.WriteLine($"{customer} ordered {quantity} items at {unitPrice:C} each. Total = {total:C}. Paid = {isPaid}");
Console.WriteLine($"Band: {size}");
Console.WriteLine($"Valid quantity: {hasValidQuantity}; can fulfil: {canFulfil}");
Console.WriteLine($"Batch quantity: {totalQuantity}");
Console.WriteLine("STAGE 01 PASS — syntax, control flow and methods");

static decimal CalculateTotal(int quantity, decimal unitPrice)
{
    if (quantity <= 0) throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(quantity));
    if (unitPrice < 0) throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(unitPrice));
    return quantity * unitPrice;
}

static string ClassifyOrder(decimal total) => total switch
{
    >= 500m => "VIP",
    >= 100m => "Standard large",
    _ => "Small"
};

3. Variables and Data Types

○
Simple picture

A variable is a labelled box. Its type says what kind of value the box is allowed to hold.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

C# is statically typed: the compiler knows each expression's type and rejects incompatible operations before the program runs. Choose types for meaning as well as size—especially decimal for business money.

Watch for this

Do not treat double and decimal as interchangeable. Binary floating point is excellent for scientific calculation but can surprise financial equality checks.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain Variables and Data Types, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

Replace Program.cs with:

csharp
string customerName = "Michael";
int quantity = 2;
decimal unitPrice = 49.99m;
bool isPaid = false;

Console.WriteLine(customerName);
Console.WriteLine(quantity);
Console.WriteLine(unitPrice);
Console.WriteLine(isPaid);

Run it.

Core types

TypeExampleMeaning
string"Michael"text
int10whole number
long8_000_000_000very large whole number
double1.82floating-point number
decimal49.99mdecimal precision; common for money
booltruetrue/false
char'A'single character
DateTimeDateTime.Nowdate/time

Why decimal for money?

Because financial calculations usually need decimal precision rather than binary floating-point approximation.

csharp
decimal price = 19.99m;

The m suffix means decimal.

4. var

○
Simple picture

var asks the compiler to write the obvious type name for you; it does not remove the type.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

Local-variable type inference happens at compile time from the right-hand expression. The resulting variable has one fixed static type, exactly as if that type had been written explicitly.

Watch for this

Do not confuse var with dynamic. dynamic postpones member checking until runtime; var does not.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain var, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

C# can infer a local variable's type:

csharp
var name = "Michael";   // string
var age = 30;           // int
var price = 10.5m;      // decimal

But C# is still statically typed.

This fails:

csharp
var age = 30;
age = "thirty";

Interview answer

What is var?

“

var is compile-time type inference. The variable still has a concrete static type; the compiler simply infers it from the assigned expression.

Do not confuse var with dynamic.

5. Strings and String Interpolation

○
Simple picture

Interpolation is a sentence template with safe holes for values or expressions.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

A $ before a string enables {expression} placeholders. Formatting such as {total:C} belongs to presentation; keep core money values as numbers until the boundary.

Watch for this

Repeated string concatenation inside a large loop creates many intermediate strings; use StringBuilder when that cost actually matters.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain Strings and String Interpolation, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

Old-looking style:

csharp
Console.WriteLine("Customer " + customerName + " ordered " + quantity);

Cleaner:

csharp
Console.WriteLine(
    $"Customer {customerName} ordered {quantity} items."
);

You can put expressions inside:

csharp
decimal total = quantity * unitPrice;

Console.WriteLine($"Total: £{total}");

6. Operators

○
Simple picture

Operators are tiny verbs: add, compare, combine conditions or change a value.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

Arithmetic operators produce values, comparison operators produce bool, and logical operators combine booleans. && and || short-circuit, so the right side may not execute.

Watch for this

Integer division truncates: 10 / 3 is 3. Make one operand floating-point or decimal when you need a fractional result.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain Operators, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

Arithmetic

csharp
int a = 10;
int b = 3;

Console.WriteLine(a + b);
Console.WriteLine(a - b);
Console.WriteLine(a * b);
Console.WriteLine(a / b);
Console.WriteLine(a % b);

% means remainder.

Example:

csharp
int number = 8;
bool isEven = number % 2 == 0;

Comparison

text
==   equal
!=   not equal
>    greater than
<    less than
>=   greater than or equal
<=   less than or equal

Logical

text
&&   AND
||   OR
!    NOT

Example:

csharp
bool hasStock = true;
bool paymentValid = true;

if (hasStock && paymentValid)
{
    Console.WriteLine("Order can proceed.");
}

7. if / else

○
Simple picture

An if statement is a fork in the road: evaluate one yes/no question and choose a branch.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

Conditions must be boolean expressions. Order overlapping branches from most specific to least specific because only the first matching branch runs.

Watch for this

Deeply nested conditionals hide the business rule. Prefer guard clauses or named methods when nesting makes the decision difficult to say aloud.

Without looking: explain if / else, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

{
    Console.WriteLine("Free delivery");
}
else
{
    Console.WriteLine("Delivery charge applies");
}

Multiple branches:

csharp
decimal total = 250m;

if (total >= 500m)
{
    Console.WriteLine("VIP order");
}
else if (total >= 100m)
{
    Console.WriteLine("Standard large order");
}
else
{
    Console.WriteLine("Small order");
}

9. switch

○
Simple picture

switch is a clearly labelled set of doors for one value or shape.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

A statement performs branch bodies; a switch expression returns a value. Modern pattern matching can test types, properties and guards while the compiler checks exhaustiveness in useful cases.

Watch for this

Always consider the unknown/default case. External values and future enum members can reach code you thought was complete.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain switch, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

csharp
string status = "paid";

switch (status)
{
    case "paid":
        Console.WriteLine("Prepare for fulfilment");
        break;

    case "pending":
        Console.WriteLine("Wait for payment");
        break;

    case "cancelled":
        Console.WriteLine("Do not fulfil");
        break;

    default:
        Console.WriteLine("Unknown status");
        break;
}

Modern switch expression:

csharp
string message = status switch
{
    "paid" => "Prepare for fulfilment",
    "pending" => "Wait for payment",
    "cancelled" => "Do not fulfil",
    _ => "Unknown status"
};

You mainly need to recognise modern switch expressions.

10. Loops

○
Simple picture

Loops repeat a job: for counts, foreach visits, and while continues while a condition remains true.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

Choose the loop that expresses intent. foreach is safest for traversal; for is useful for indices; while fits condition-driven repetition. break exits and continue skips one iteration.

Watch for this

Changing a collection while enumerating it commonly throws. Also check that a while loop changes the state used by its condition.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain Loops, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

for

csharp
for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++)
{
    Console.WriteLine(i);
}

Think:

MENTAL MODEL
start → condition → body → increment

while

csharp
int attempts = 0;

while (attempts < 3)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"Attempt {attempts + 1}");
    attempts++;
}

foreach

Very common:

csharp
string[] customers =
{
    "Michael",
    "Sarah",
    "John"
};

foreach (string customer in customers)
{
    Console.WriteLine(customer);
}

break

Stops the loop.

csharp
foreach (string customer in customers)
{
    if (customer == "Sarah")
    {
        break;
    }

    Console.WriteLine(customer);
}

continue

Skips the current iteration.

csharp
foreach (string customer in customers)
{
    if (customer == "Sarah")
    {
        continue;
    }

    Console.WriteLine(customer);
}

11. Methods

○
Simple picture

A method gives a name to a small job, with input doors called parameters and an output door called the return value.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

A method signature is its name plus parameter types and modifiers. Return types make outputs explicit; void means the effect is observable elsewhere rather than returned.

Watch for this

A method that calculates, saves, logs and emails is several jobs disguised as one. Small coherent methods are easier to test and explain.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain Methods, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

Methods package behaviour into reusable units.

csharp
void PrintWelcome()
{
    Console.WriteLine("Welcome to OrderFlow");
}

PrintWelcome();

Parameters

csharp
void PrintCustomer(string name)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"Customer: {name}");
}

PrintCustomer("Michael");

name is a parameter.

"Michael" is an argument.

Return values

csharp
decimal CalculateTotal(int quantity, decimal unitPrice)
{
    return quantity * unitPrice;
}

decimal total = CalculateTotal(3, 25m);

void

Means no returned value.

csharp
void PrintOrder(decimal total)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"Order total: £{total}");
}

Expression-bodied method

csharp
decimal CalculateTotal(int quantity, decimal price)
    => quantity * price;

tutorial-snapshots/01-console/Program.cs · csharp
static decimal ApplyDiscount(decimal total, decimal percentage)
{
    if (total < 0m) throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(total));
    if (percentage is < 0m or > 100m) throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(percentage));
    return total - (total * percentage / 100m);
}

These snippets are loaded from the downloadable solution that was built, migrated and tested locally. Type them rather than merely reading them. Lesson snippets isolate one idea and sometimes show an earlier, smaller Order shape; this checkpoint is the canonical cumulative version after refactoring, so do not paste every sketch into the final solution.

tutorial-snapshots/02-domain-linq/Domain/Order.cs
namespace OrderFlow.Stage02.Domain;

public sealed class Order
{
    private readonly List<OrderLine> _lines = [];

    public Order(string customer)
    {
        if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(customer))
            throw new ArgumentException("Customer is required.", nameof(customer));

        Id = Guid.NewGuid();
        Customer = customer.Trim();
    }

    public Guid Id { get; }
    public string Customer { get; }
    public bool IsPaid { get; private set; }
    public IReadOnlyList<OrderLine> Lines => _lines;
    public decimal Total => _lines.Sum(line => line.LineTotal);

    public void AddLine(string product, int quantity, decimal unitPrice) =>
        _lines.Add(new OrderLine(product, quantity, unitPrice));

    public void MarkPaid()
    {
        if (_lines.Count == 0)
            throw new InvalidOperationException("An empty order cannot be paid.");

        IsPaid = true;
    }
}
tutorial-snapshots/02-domain-linq/Infrastructure/InMemoryOrderRepository.cs
using OrderFlow.Stage02.Application;
using OrderFlow.Stage02.Domain;

namespace OrderFlow.Stage02.Infrastructure;

public sealed class InMemoryOrderRepository : IOrderRepository
{
    private readonly Dictionary<Guid, Order> _orders = [];

    public void Add(Order order)
    {
        if (!_orders.TryAdd(order.Id, order))
            throw new InvalidOperationException($"Order {order.Id} already exists.");
    }

    public Order? Find(Guid id) => _orders.GetValueOrDefault(id);

    public IReadOnlyList<Order> List() => _orders.Values.ToList();
}
tutorial-snapshots/02-domain-linq/Program.cs
using OrderFlow.Stage02.Application;
using OrderFlow.Stage02.Domain;
using OrderFlow.Stage02.Infrastructure;

IOrderRepository repository = new InMemoryOrderRepository();

var first = NewOrder("Ada", "Keyboard", 2, 40m, paid: true);
var second = NewOrder("Grace", "Monitor", 1, 125m, paid: true);
var third = NewOrder("Linus", "Cable", 2, 15m, paid: false);

first.AddLine("Mouse", 1, 10m);

repository.Add(first);
repository.Add(second);
repository.Add(third);

var highValuePaidOrders = repository.List()
    .Where(order => order.IsPaid && order.Total >= 75m)
    .OrderByDescending(order => order.Total)
    .Select(order => new { order.Customer, order.Total })
    .ToList();

if (highValuePaidOrders.Count != 2 || highValuePaidOrders[0].Customer != "Grace")
    throw new InvalidOperationException("The Stage 02 LINQ self-check failed.");

foreach (var order in highValuePaidOrders)
    Console.WriteLine($"{order.Customer}: {order.Total:C}");

Console.WriteLine("STAGE 02 PASS — objects, interface, collections and LINQ");

static Order NewOrder(
    string customer,
    string product,
    int quantity,
    decimal unitPrice,
    bool paid)
{
    var order = new Order(customer);
    order.AddLine(product, quantity, unitPrice);
    if (paid)
        order.MarkPaid();
    return order;
}

12. Classes and Objects

○
Simple picture

A class is a blueprint; an object is one house built from that blueprint.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

A class defines state and behaviour. new creates an instance with its own state, while the type determines which members the compiler permits.

Watch for this

Do not make every data shape a behaviour-heavy class. DTOs and immutable records can be better when the job is simply carrying data.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain Classes and Objects, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

text

Add:

public class Order
{
    public int Id { get; set; }

    public string CustomerName { get; set; } = "";

    public decimal Amount { get; set; }

    public bool IsPaid { get; set; }

13. Fields vs Properties

○
Simple picture

A field is storage inside the object; a property is a controlled doorway to that storage or calculated value.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

Properties compile to accessor methods and form the normal public surface of .NET models. They can validate, calculate, restrict setters or be init-only.

Watch for this

Public fields expose representation directly and make later validation difficult. Avoid clever property getters with surprising I/O or expensive work.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain Fields vs Properties, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

A field:

csharp
private decimal _amount;

A property:

csharp
public decimal Amount { get; set; }

Properties are the normal public-facing mechanism for exposing object state.

A property can control access:

csharp
public decimal Amount { get; private set; }

Outside code can read the amount but cannot directly assign it.

14. Constructors

○
Simple picture

A constructor is the object's setup checklist: it prevents a half-built object from leaving the factory.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

Constructors establish invariants by requiring dependencies and essential values. C# can overload constructors, but each path should create a valid instance.

Watch for this

Do not inject optional clutter or perform network/database work in constructors. Construction should be predictable and fast.

        Amount = amount;

15. Methods Inside Classes

○
Simple picture

Methods inside a class are the actions that belong with that object's knowledge.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

Instance methods receive an implicit this reference and can use instance state. Behaviour should live near the invariant it protects, not merely near the screen that called it.

Watch for this

Avoid anemic models by putting every rule in one giant service, but also avoid forcing infrastructure work into domain objects.

we provide meaningful behaviour.

16. Encapsulation

○
Simple picture

Encapsulation is a protective case: callers use safe controls instead of touching delicate parts directly.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

Hide representation, expose intention-revealing operations and keep invariants true after every public call. This reduces the number of states the rest of the program must handle.

Watch for this

Private setters alone do not guarantee encapsulation. If a public list can be modified freely, callers can still break the object's rules.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain Encapsulation, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

Encapsulation means:

“

Keep an object's internal state controlled and expose meaningful operations.

Bad:

csharp
public decimal Balance;

Better:

csharp
public class Wallet
{
    public decimal Balance { get; private set; }

    public void AddMoney(decimal amount)
    {
        if (amount <= 0)
        {
            throw new ArgumentException(
                "Amount must be positive"
            );
        }

        Balance += amount;
    }
}

The class protects its rules.

17. Access Modifiers

○
Simple picture

Access modifiers decide who receives a key: everyone, this class, this assembly or inheritors.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

public, private, protected, internal and combinations define the compile-time visibility boundary. Default to the narrowest access that supports the design.

Watch for this

protected creates a long-term contract for subclasses. Exposing internals ‘just in case’ increases coupling and testing surface.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain Access Modifiers, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

public

Accessible from other code.

public string CustomerName { get; set; }

private

Only inside the class.

csharp
private decimal _internalFee;

protected

Inside the class and derived classes.

internal

Within the same assembly/project.

For tomorrow, know public, private, protected confidently.

18. static

○
Simple picture

static means the member belongs to the type itself, not to one particular object.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

Static members have one type-level identity per load context and cannot directly access instance members. They suit pure helpers, constants and carefully controlled shared services.

Watch for this

Mutable static state is global state: tests influence one another, concurrency becomes harder and lifetime is hidden.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain static, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

Instance method:

csharp
order.MarkAsPaid();

Static method:

csharp
public static class PriceCalculator
{
    public static decimal AddVat(
        decimal amount,
        decimal rate)
    {
        return amount + (amount * rate);
    }
}

Call:

csharp
decimal withVat =
    PriceCalculator.AddVat(100m, 0.20m);

No object is required.

19. Inheritance

○
Simple picture

Inheritance says one specialised thing is substitutable for a more general thing.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

A derived class receives accessible base behaviour and can extend or override virtual members. Use it for a stable ‘is-a’ relationship, not just to reuse code.

Watch for this

Prefer composition when behaviours vary independently. Deep inheritance trees create fragile coupling and often violate substitutability.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain Inheritance, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

        int id,
        string customerName,
        decimal amount)
        : base(id, customerName, amount)
    {
    }
}

Read:

text
PremiumOrder IS AN Order

Inheritance models an is-a relationship.

Do not force inheritance where composition is more natural.

20. Polymorphism

○
Simple picture

Polymorphism lets one instruction work with many shapes because each shape knows how to perform its version.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

Code calls through a base type or interface while runtime dispatch selects the concrete override. This moves branching out of the caller and into replaceable implementations.

Watch for this

A big switch on concrete types is often missed polymorphism, but polymorphism is not automatically better for simple finite data cases.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain Polymorphism, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

Example:

csharp
public abstract class PaymentProcessor
{
    public abstract void Pay(decimal amount);
}

Stripe:

csharp
public class StripePaymentProcessor
    : PaymentProcessor
{
    public override void Pay(decimal amount)
    {
        Console.WriteLine(
            $"Stripe charged £{amount}"
        );
    }
}

PayPal:

csharp
public class PayPalPaymentProcessor
    : PaymentProcessor
{
    public override void Pay(decimal amount)
    {
        Console.WriteLine(
            $"PayPal charged £{amount}"
        );
    }
}

Then:

csharp
List<PaymentProcessor> processors =
[
    new StripePaymentProcessor(),
    new PayPalPaymentProcessor()
];

foreach (PaymentProcessor processor in processors)
{
    processor.Pay(100m);
}

The caller works with the abstraction; each implementation behaves differently.

That is polymorphism.

21. Overloading vs Overriding

○
Simple picture

Overloading reuses a method name for different inputs; overriding replaces inherited behaviour for a subtype.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

Overload selection is compile-time and based on the call signature. Override dispatch is runtime and requires a virtual/abstract base member plus override.

Watch for this

Hiding a member with new is not overriding. Also avoid overload sets where null or implicit conversions make the intended call unclear.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain Overloading vs Overriding, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

Overloading

Same method name, different parameter signature:

csharp
public decimal Calculate(decimal price)
{
    return price;
}

public decimal Calculate(
    decimal price,
    decimal discount)
{
    return price - discount;
}

Overriding

Derived class replaces virtual/abstract behaviour:

csharp
public override void Pay(decimal amount)
{
    Console.WriteLine("Custom payment logic");
}

Interview memory

MENTAL MODEL
Overload  → same name, different parameters
Override  → derived class replaces inherited behaviour

22. Interfaces

○
Simple picture

An interface is a promise: ‘anything that signs this contract can do these operations.’

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

Interfaces describe capabilities without choosing the implementation. They create a seam for substitution, testing and dependency inversion; a class may implement several interfaces.

Watch for this

Do not create an interface for every class automatically. Extract one when there is a real boundary, multiple behaviour choices or a useful test seam.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain Interfaces, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

Interfaces are extremely important for ASP.NET Core.

Create:

text
IPaymentService.cs
csharp
public interface IPaymentService
{
    Task PayAsync(decimal amount);
}

Implementation:

csharp
public class StripePaymentService
    : IPaymentService
{
    public async Task PayAsync(decimal amount)
    {
        await Task.Delay(100);

        Console.WriteLine(
            $"Stripe processed £{amount}"
        );
    }
}

Another:

csharp
public class FakePaymentService
    : IPaymentService
{
    public async Task PayAsync(decimal amount)
    {
        await Task.Delay(10);

        Console.WriteLine(
            $"FAKE PAYMENT: £{amount}"
        );
    }
}

Now code can depend on:

text
IPaymentService

rather than Stripe directly.

That gives us:

text
loose coupling
testability
replaceable implementations
Dependency Injection

We will return to this.

23. Abstract Classes

○
Simple picture

An abstract class is a partly built base model: it can provide shared machinery but cannot be used directly.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

It may hold state, constructors and implemented members as well as abstract members. Choose it when related implementations share identity and protected behaviour; choose an interface for a capability contract.

Watch for this

A base class consumes the single class-inheritance slot and couples descendants to its evolution. Shared code alone is not enough reason.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain Abstract Classes, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

Example:

csharp
public abstract class Notification
{
    public string Recipient { get; }

    protected Notification(string recipient)
    {
        Recipient = recipient;
    }

    public abstract Task SendAsync();

    public void Log()
    {
        Console.WriteLine(
            $"Sending to {Recipient}"
        );
    }
}

An abstract class can provide:

  • shared state;
  • constructors;
  • implemented methods;
  • abstract methods.

Interview: interface vs abstract class

Good answer:

“

An interface primarily expresses a contract/capability and allows unrelated implementations to be substituted. An abstract class is useful when closely related types need shared implementation or state in addition to polymorphism.

24. Arrays

○
Simple picture

An array is a numbered row of fixed lockers, all holding the same type.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

Arrays have fixed length, contiguous indexed storage and O(1) index access. They are ideal when size is known or an API specifically expects an array.

Watch for this

The last valid index is Length - 1. If the collection must grow frequently, use List<T> instead.

25. List<T>

○
Simple picture

List<T> is a resizable ordered shelf that keeps insertion order and supports index access.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

It is backed by an array that occasionally grows. Appending is amortised O(1); searching by value is O(n); inserting near the front shifts elements.

Watch for this

Using List<T> for repeated membership checks can create accidental O(n²) work. Consider HashSet<T> or Dictionary when lookup is the real task.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain List<T>, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

Resizable ordered collection:

csharp
List<Order> orders = new List<Order>();

orders.Add(
    new Order(1, "Michael", 100m)
);

orders.Add(
    new Order(2, "Sarah", 250m)
);

Console.WriteLine(orders.Count);

Modern syntax:

csharp
List<int> numbers =
[
    1,
    2,
    3
];

26. Dictionary<TKey,TValue>

○
Simple picture

A dictionary is a labelled cupboard: give it a unique key and retrieve the matching value quickly.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

Dictionary<TKey,TValue> is hash-based and provides average O(1) add/find/remove when keys have stable equality and hash codes.

Watch for this

Duplicate keys throw when using Add; index assignment replaces. Mutable keys and incorrect equality implementations break lookup assumptions.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain Dictionary<TKey,TValue>, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

Key/value lookup:

csharp
Dictionary<int, Order> ordersById =
    new Dictionary<int, Order>();

ordersById[1] =
    new Order(1, "Michael", 100m);

Safer retrieval:

csharp
if (ordersById.TryGetValue(
        1,
        out Order? order))
{
    Console.WriteLine(order.CustomerName);
}

Mental model:

MENTAL MODEL
key → value
1   → Order

Average lookup is typically O(1).

Very important for DSA.

Simple picture

A hash set is a guest list: it cares whether a value is present, not how many times it arrived.

Technical truth

HashSet<T> stores unique values with average O(1) membership operations and supports set union, intersection and difference.

30. Generics

○
Simple picture

Generics are reusable moulds with a type-shaped opening, so one design safely works for many types.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

A generic type or method is compiled with type parameters and checked without casting. Constraints such as where T : class describe required capabilities.

Watch for this

Avoid replacing meaningful domain operations with an over-general generic abstraction that saves a few lines but hides intent.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain Generics, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

CSHARP FRAGMENT · NOT STANDALONE
List<Order>
Dictionary<int, Order>
HashSet<string>

You can make your own:

csharp
public class Result<T>
{
    public bool Success { get; set; }

    public T? Data { get; set; }

    public string? Error { get; set; }
}

Use:

csharp
Result<Order> result =
    new Result<Order>();

Generics give:

  • reuse;
  • type safety;
  • less casting;
  • clearer APIs.

tutorial-snapshots/02-domain-linq/Infrastructure/InMemoryOrderRepository.cs · csharp
public sealed class InMemoryOrderRepository : IOrderRepository
{
    private readonly Dictionary<Guid, Order> _orders = [];

    public void Add(Order order)
    {
        if (!_orders.TryAdd(order.Id, order))
            throw new InvalidOperationException($"Order {order.Id} already exists.");
    }

    public Order? Find(Guid id) => _orders.GetValueOrDefault(id);
    public IReadOnlyList<Order> List() => _orders.Values.ToList();
}

31. Nullable Reference Types

○
Simple picture

Nullable reference types are warning labels that distinguish ‘should contain an object’ from ‘may be empty.’

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

The feature is compile-time flow analysis, not a runtime wrapper. string and string? are the same CLR type, but annotations let the compiler warn about unsafe dereferences.

Watch for this

Null can still arrive from older libraries, deserialisation or incorrect suppression. ! silences analysis; it does not prove a value exists.

? communicates:

null is an expected possibility.

Without it, modern C# may warn when null is assigned to a non-nullable reference.

32. Null Conditional

○
Simple picture

?. says ‘continue only if the object exists; otherwise produce null.’

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

Null-conditional access short-circuits the remaining member or index operation and lifts the result to a nullable shape when necessary.

Watch for this

Do not scatter ?. everywhere to hide invalid state. Required data should be validated at the boundary.

33. Null Coalescing

○
Simple picture

?? supplies a spare value when the first value is null.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

Null coalescing evaluates the right operand only when needed. ??= assigns a fallback only when the target is currently null.

Watch for this

A convenient fallback can hide missing required data. Decide whether absence is valid, recoverable or an error.

34. Exceptions

○
Simple picture

An exception is an emergency message that travels up the call stack until suitable code handles it.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

Use exceptions for exceptional failure, preserve stack traces with throw;, catch where you can add context or recover, and convert failures to boundary-appropriate responses centrally.

Watch for this

Never catch Exception merely to ignore it. Exceptions are also expensive and unclear as ordinary branching mechanisms.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain Exceptions, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

csharp
try
{
    int number = int.Parse("hello");
}
catch (FormatException)
{
    Console.WriteLine("Invalid number");
}

General:

csharp
try
{
    // risky operation
}
catch (Exception ex)
{
    Console.WriteLine(ex.Message);
}
finally
{
    Console.WriteLine("Always runs");
}

Throwing:

csharp
if (amount <= 0)
{
    throw new ArgumentException(
        "Amount must be greater than zero"
    );
}

Interview principle

Do not say:

“

“I wrap everything in try/catch.”

Handle exceptions where you can meaningfully:

  • recover;
  • translate to another error;
  • log;
  • return an appropriate API response.

35. using and IDisposable

○
Simple picture

using is a promise to return a borrowed resource even if something goes wrong.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

IDisposable.Dispose releases deterministic resources such as streams, handles and scopes. A using statement/declaration compiles to a try/finally; await using supports IAsyncDisposable.

Watch for this

Garbage collection manages memory, not timely release of external resources. Do not dispose an object owned by the DI container.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain using and IDisposable, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

Example:

csharp
using FileStream stream =
    File.OpenRead("orders.txt");

Dispose() is called when the scope ends.

Interview question

If .NET has garbage collection, why do we need Dispose?

Strong answer:

“

GC manages managed memory, but some resources need deterministic cleanup — for example streams, handles, database connections, or unmanaged resources. IDisposable provides that deterministic cleanup.

37. LINQ

○
Simple picture

LINQ is a pipeline: choose items, reshape them, order them and finally collect the result.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

Standard query operators compose over IEnumerable<T> or IQueryable<T>. Operators such as Where and Select describe transformations; terminal operations enumerate or aggregate.

Watch for this

A readable one-pass pipeline can become repeated database queries or multiple enumeration. Know when execution happens.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain LINQ, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

LINQ = Language Integrated Query.

Create:

csharp
List<Order> orders =
[
    new Order(1, "Michael", 100m),
    new Order(2, "Sarah", 250m),
    new Order(3, "John", 75m)
];

Where

Filter:

csharp
var largeOrders =
    orders.Where(
        order => order.Amount >= 100m
    );

Select

Transform/project:

csharp
var customerNames =
    orders.Select(
        order => order.CustomerName
    );

OrderBy

csharp
var ordered =
    orders.OrderBy(
        order => order.Amount
    );

Descending:

csharp
var expensiveFirst =
    orders.OrderByDescending(
        order => order.Amount
    );

Any

csharp
bool hasLargeOrders =
    orders.Any(
        order => order.Amount > 200m
    );

All

csharp
bool allPositive =
    orders.All(
        order => order.Amount > 0m
    );

FirstOrDefault

csharp
Order? order =
    orders.FirstOrDefault(
        order => order.Id == 2
    );

SingleOrDefault

csharp
Order? order =
    orders.SingleOrDefault(
        order => order.Id == 2
    );

Difference:

MENTAL MODEL
FirstOrDefault  → first match
SingleOrDefault → expects zero or one; throws if multiple

Count

csharp
int count =
    orders.Count(
        order => order.Amount >= 100m
    );

GroupBy

csharp
var groups =
    orders.GroupBy(
        order => order.IsPaid
    );

Projection

Later in EF Core, this becomes very important:

csharp
var summaries =
    orders.Select(
        order => new
        {
            order.Id,
            order.CustomerName,
            order.Amount
        }
    );

38. Method Chaining

○
Simple picture

Method chaining reads like water flowing through connected filters, with each operation returning the next input.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

Each call returns a value that exposes the next operator. LINQ chains remain composable because sequence operators return sequence abstractions.

Watch for this

Long chains with side effects are difficult to debug. Break named business stages into variables or methods.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain Method Chaining, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

    orders
        .Where(o => o.Amount >= 100m)
        .OrderByDescending(o => o.Amount)
        .Select(o => o.CustomerName)
        .ToList();

Read it in English:

“

Take orders → keep orders ≥ £100 → sort highest first → select names → materialise into a List.

This reading technique makes LINQ much easier.

39. Deferred Execution

○
Simple picture

Deferred execution is a recipe card: writing the query does not cook the meal; enumeration does.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

Many LINQ operators return an iterator that re-runs against the current source on each enumeration. ToList, ToArray, Count and similar operations materialise or consume it.

Watch for this

Changing the source before enumeration changes results; enumerating an EF query repeatedly can hit the database repeatedly.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain Deferred Execution, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

csharp
var query =
    orders.Where(
        o => o.Amount >= 100m
    );

This may represent a query rather than immediately creating a result list.

When you do:

csharp
var result = query.ToList();

you materialise it.

This becomes important with EF Core.

40. IEnumerable<T>

○
Simple picture

IEnumerable<T> is a promise that items can be visited one at a time.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

It exposes GetEnumerator and supports streaming iteration without requiring count or index access. LINQ-to-Objects extension methods target it.

Watch for this

It says nothing about cheap repeat enumeration. Do not assume every enumerable is an in-memory list.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain IEnumerable<T>, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

IEnumerable<T> represents something that can be enumerated.

csharp

{
    return orders;
}

You can:

csharp
foreach (Order order in GetOrders())
{
    Console.WriteLine(order.Amount);
}

Later:

text
IEnumerable<T>
vs
IQueryable<T>

will matter when databases enter the picture.

41. Delegates

○
Simple picture

A delegate is a type-safe variable that can point to a compatible method.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

Delegates store an invocation list. Action represents no return value; Func<...,TResult> includes a return value; custom delegates communicate domain meaning.

Watch for this

Delegates can capture object lifetimes through closures. Unclear chains of callbacks can make control flow difficult to trace.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain Delegates, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

A delegate is a type-safe reference to a method.

csharp
public delegate void MessageHandler(
    string message
);

Method:

csharp
void PrintMessage(string message)
{
    Console.WriteLine(message);
}

Assign:

csharp
MessageHandler handler = PrintMessage;

handler("Hello");

Built-in delegates are more common.

Action

No return value:

csharp
Action<string> log =
    message => Console.WriteLine(message);

Func

Returns a value:

csharp
Func<int, int, int> add =
    (a, b) => a + b;

Last generic type = return type.

42. Events

○
Simple picture

An event is a bell: a publisher rings it and any subscribed listeners react without the publisher knowing them.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

Events wrap multicast delegates so outside code can subscribe/unsubscribe but cannot normally invoke the event. They provide in-process observer-style decoupling.

Watch for this

Long-lived publishers keep subscribers alive. Unsubscribe when lifetimes differ, and do not confuse in-process events with durable distributed messaging.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain Events, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

Simple publisher/subscriber:

csharp
public class OrderEvents
{
    public event Action<Order>? OrderCreated;

    public void RaiseCreated(Order order)
    {
        OrderCreated?.Invoke(order);
    }
}

Subscribe:

csharp
OrderEvents events = new();

events.OrderCreated += order =>
{
    Console.WriteLine(
        $"Created order {order.Id}"
    );
};

You only need the concept tonight:

MENTAL MODEL
publisher raises event
       ↓
subscribers react

Add this layer

  1. Put create, read and pay use cases in OrderService.

Run itdotnet run --project tutorial-snapshots/03-async-service
Proof of understanding

Trace MarkPaidAsync from caller to repository and receipt sender. Identify which awaits represent I/O, why .Result is dangerous, and what happens if saving succeeds but sending the receipt fails.

Honest boundary

Production truth: this small sample prevents a second receipt after a fully successful retry, but saving Paid and sending the receipt are not one atomic operation. If the save succeeds and sending fails, a retry sees Paid and may skip the receipt. A production design closes that gap with a transactional outbox, durable delivery and an idempotent consumer; Chapter 6 explains that evolution.

Verified milestone code

These snippets are loaded from the downloadable solution that was built, migrated and tested locally. Type them rather than merely reading them. Lesson snippets isolate one idea and sometimes show an earlier, smaller Order shape; this checkpoint is the canonical cumulative version after refactoring, so do not paste every sketch into the final solution.

tutorial-snapshots/03-async-service/Application/OrderService.cs
using OrderFlow.Stage03.Domain;

namespace OrderFlow.Stage03.Application;

public sealed class OrderService(
    IOrderRepository repository,
    IReceiptSender receiptSender,
    TimeProvider clock)
{
    public async Task<Order> CreateAsync(
        string customer,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        var order = new Order(customer, clock.GetUtcNow());
        await repository.AddAsync(order, cancellationToken);
        await repository.SaveChangesAsync(cancellationToken);
        return order;
    }

    public Task<Order?> GetAsync(Guid id, CancellationToken cancellationToken) =>
        repository.FindAsync(id, cancellationToken);

    public async Task<Order> MarkPaidAsync(
        Guid id,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        var order = await repository.FindAsync(id, cancellationToken)
            ?? throw new KeyNotFoundException($"Order {id} was not found.");

        if (order.MarkPaid())
        {
            await repository.SaveChangesAsync(cancellationToken);
            await receiptSender.SendAsync(order, cancellationToken);
        }

        return order;
    }
}
tutorial-snapshots/03-async-service/Program.cs
using OrderFlow.Stage03.Application;
using OrderFlow.Stage03.Infrastructure;

using var timeout = new CancellationTokenSource(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5));
var repository = new InMemoryAsyncOrderRepository();
var receipts = new SpyReceiptSender();
var service = new OrderService(repository, receipts, TimeProvider.System);

var order = await service.CreateAsync("Ada", timeout.Token);
order.AddLine("Keyboard", 2, 40m);

// These operations are independent. Creating both tasks first lets WhenAll
// compose their completion; WhenAll itself does not start the work.
var firstRead = service.GetAsync(order.Id, timeout.Token);
var secondRead = service.GetAsync(order.Id, timeout.Token);
var reads = await Task.WhenAll(firstRead, secondRead);

await service.MarkPaidAsync(order.Id, timeout.Token);
await service.MarkPaidAsync(order.Id, timeout.Token);

if (reads.Any(result => result is null) || receipts.SendCount != 1)
    throw new InvalidOperationException("The Stage 03 async/idempotency self-check failed.");

Console.WriteLine($"{order.Customer}: {order.Total:C} | Paid: {order.IsPaid}");
Console.WriteLine("STAGE 03 PASS — async, cancellation and retry-safe state transition");

43. Why Async Exists

○
Simple picture

Async lets a worker start waiting for slow outside work and give the thread back instead of standing idle.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

For I/O, an awaited operation uses Task to represent future completion and releases the current thread while the OS/device works. This improves responsiveness and server throughput, not necessarily single-operation speed.

Watch for this

async does not automatically create a new thread. CPU-heavy work still consumes CPU and may require a deliberate parallelism strategy.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain Why Async Exists, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

Imagine your Web API is waiting on a database.

Synchronous thinking:

MENTAL MODEL
request thread
   ↓
send DB query
   ↓
WAIT
WAIT
WAIT
   ↓
DB responds

Async:

MENTAL MODEL
request
  ↓
start I/O
  ↓
await
  ↓
thread is not needlessly blocked waiting
  ↓
I/O completes
  ↓
continuation resumes

For Web APIs, this matters because requests often spend time waiting on:

  • databases;
  • HTTP APIs;
  • files;
  • queues.

44. Task

○
Simple picture

A Task is a claim ticket for work that will finish later but returns no value.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

It represents completion, failure or cancellation. Returning a task lets callers compose, await and observe the operation.

Watch for this

Fire-and-forget tasks can lose exceptions and outlive request-scoped dependencies. Await work unless lifetime is deliberately managed.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain Task, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

Represents asynchronous work.

csharp
async Task SimulateWorkAsync()
{
    await Task.Delay(1000);

    Console.WriteLine("Done");
}

Call:

csharp
await SimulateWorkAsync();

45. Task<T>

○
Simple picture

Task<T> is a claim ticket that yields a value of type T when the work finishes.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

Awaiting unwraps the result or rethrows the original failure at the await point, keeping asynchronous control flow readable.

Watch for this

Do not return Task<T> merely to look asynchronous. If there is no asynchronous operation, avoid a needless state machine.

{
    await Task.Delay(100);

    return new Order(
        1,
        "Michael",
        100m
    );
}

Use:

csharp
Order order =
    await GetOrderAsync();

46. Important Interview Point

○
Simple picture

await pauses the method, not the whole application and usually not a blocked thread.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

The compiler transforms the method into a state machine. On incomplete await, it records continuation state, returns control and resumes when the awaited operation signals completion.

Watch for this

Execution before the first incomplete await is synchronous. Shared state can still race when several operations overlap.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain Important Interview Point, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

Do not say:

“

“async creates another thread.”

Better:

“

async/await is particularly useful for I/O-bound work. While I/O is incomplete, the application does not need to synchronously block a thread simply waiting for the result.

○
Simple picture

.Result and .Wait() force someone to stand at the counter instead of returning when the order is ready.

Technical truth

They synchronously block a thread and can deadlock in certain synchronization contexts or reduce ASP.NET throughput through thread starvation. Prefer async all the way.

There are rare synchronous boundaries, but wrapping everything in Task.Run is not a universal fix.

48. Task.WhenAll

○
Simple picture

WhenAll watches several already-started independent tasks and continues after every one has finished.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

Create or obtain the tasks before awaiting the combined task. Task.WhenAll composes their completion; it does not itself start the work. Total latency can approach the slowest operation rather than their sum, subject to resource limits.

Watch for this

Parallelise only independent work. Unbounded fan-out can overwhelm the database or downstream service.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain Task.WhenAll, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

Independent calls:

csharp
Task<Order> first =
    GetOrderAsync();

Task<Order> second =
    GetOrderAsync();

await Task.WhenAll(
    first,
    second
);

Useful when operations do not depend on one another.

49. CancellationToken

○
Simple picture

A cancellation token is a polite stop request passed through every layer; it is not a thread kill switch.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

Operations observe CancellationToken, stop cooperatively and normally throw OperationCanceledException. ASP.NET exposes request-abort cancellation that should flow to EF and HTTP calls.

Watch for this

Catching cancellation as an ordinary error creates noisy logs. Do not claim cancellation support while ignoring the token downstream.

Without looking: explain CancellationToken, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

    CancellationToken cancellationToken)
{
    await Task.Delay(
        5000,
        cancellationToken
    );
}

Mental model:

“

Allow work to stop when it is no longer needed.

In ASP.NET Core, cancellation often flows from the incoming request down into database and HTTP operations.

○
Simple picture

.NET compilation
   ↓
Intermediate Language
   ↓
CLR

machine execution

The CLR provides runtime services including:

  • execution;
  • JIT compilation;
  • garbage collection;
  • exception handling;

53. IL

○
Simple picture

IL is the portable instruction language between your C# source and a particular CPU's machine code.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

The compiler emits Common Intermediate Language plus metadata into assemblies. This common form supports multiple .NET languages and later JIT/AOT compilation.

Watch for this

IL is lower-level than C# but is not generally the native instruction set executed directly by the processor.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain IL, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

C# does not normally compile straight from source into a final machine-code executable in the same conceptual way as a traditional native compiler.

It compiles into Intermediate Language plus metadata inside assemblies.

Then the runtime executes it.

Interview shorthand:

MENTAL MODEL
C# → IL → CLR/JIT → machine code

56. Garbage Collection

○
Simple picture

The garbage collector is a caretaker that finds managed objects no reachable code can use and reclaims their memory.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

.NET uses a generational, tracing GC. Short-lived objects usually die in generation 0; surviving objects may be promoted; large objects have a separate heap strategy.

Watch for this

GC handles managed memory, not deterministic cleanup. Memory leaks still occur when references unintentionally keep objects reachable.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain Garbage Collection, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

The garbage collector manages memory for managed objects.

Simplified mental model:

MENTAL MODEL
create objects
   ↓
objects become unreachable
   ↓
GC eventually reclaims memory

You may hear about generations:

MENTAL MODEL
Gen 0 → short-lived objects
Gen 1 → intermediate
Gen 2 → longer-lived objects

Do not turn this into a GC internals lecture.

Strong interview answer:

“

.NET uses automatic garbage collection for managed memory. The GC tracks reachability and reclaims memory from objects that are no longer reachable. Objects that survive collections can be promoted through generations.

57. Value Types vs Reference Types

○
Simple picture

A value-type variable contains its value; a reference-type variable contains a route to an object.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

Assignment copies a value type's data, while reference-type assignment copies the reference so variables can observe the same object. Actual storage depends on context and runtime optimisation—not a simplistic ‘stack versus heap’ rule.

Watch for this

Mutable structs and shallow copying surprise people. Explain semantics first; avoid presenting stack/heap as the definition.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain Value Types vs Reference Types, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

Value:

csharp
int x = 10;
int y = x;

y = 20;

Console.WriteLine(x); // 10

Reference:

csharp
Order first =
    new Order(1, "Michael", 100m);

Order second = first;

// both references point to same object

Good answer:

“

Value-type assignment normally copies the value. Reference-type assignment copies the reference, so two variables can refer to the same object.

Avoid the simplistic:

“

value = stack, reference = heap

because storage details depend on context.

58. Boxing / Unboxing

○
Simple picture

Boxing puts a value-type value into an object-shaped package; unboxing takes it out with the exact expected type.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

Boxing allocates an object and copies the value. Generics usually avoid the boxing that older non-generic collections required.

Watch for this

Unboxing to the wrong value type throws even if a numeric conversion might seem reasonable. Frequent boxing can create allocation pressure.

src/OrderFlow.Api/Program.cs
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.JwtBearer;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using OrderFlow.Api;
using OrderFlow.Application;
using OrderFlow.Infrastructure;

var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

builder.Services.AddControllers();
builder.Services.AddOpenApi();
builder.Services.AddProblemDetails();
builder.Services.AddExceptionHandler<ApiExceptionHandler>();
builder.Services.AddSingleton(TimeProvider.System);
builder.Services.AddScoped<IOrderService, OrderService>();
builder.Services.AddOrderFlowInfrastructure(
    builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("Orders")
        ?? throw new InvalidOperationException("Connection string 'Orders' is missing."));

builder.Services
    .AddAuthentication(JwtBearerDefaults.AuthenticationScheme)
    .AddJwtBearer();
builder.Services.AddAuthorizationBuilder()
    .AddPolicy("OrderManager", policy => policy.RequireRole("OrderManager"));

var app = builder.Build();

app.UseExceptionHandler();

if (app.Environment.IsDevelopment())
{
    app.MapOpenApi();
    await using var scope = app.Services.CreateAsyncScope();
    await scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<OrderDbContext>()
        .Database.MigrateAsync();
}

app.UseHttpsRedirection();
app.UseAuthentication();
app.UseAuthorization();
app.MapControllers();
app.MapGet("/health", () => Results.Ok(new { status = "healthy" }));

app.Run();

src/OrderFlow.Api/Controllers/OrdersController.cs
using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using OrderFlow.Application;

namespace OrderFlow.Api.Controllers;

[ApiController]
[Route("api/orders")]
public sealed class OrdersController(IOrderService orderService) : ControllerBase
{
    [HttpGet]
    public async Task<ActionResult<IReadOnlyList<OrderDto>>> List(CancellationToken cancellationToken) =>
        Ok(await orderService.ListAsync(cancellationToken));

    [HttpGet("{id:guid}")]
    public async Task<ActionResult<OrderDto>> Get(Guid id, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        var order = await orderService.GetAsync(id, cancellationToken);
        return order is null ? NotFound() : Ok(order);
    }

    [Authorize(Policy = "OrderManager")]
    [HttpPost]
    public async Task<ActionResult<OrderDto>> Create(
        CreateOrderRequest request,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        var command = new CreateOrderCommand(
            request.Customer,
            request.Lines.Select(line => new CreateOrderLineCommand(
                line.Product,
                line.Quantity,
                line.UnitPrice)).ToList());

        var created = await orderService.CreateAsync(command, cancellationToken);
        return CreatedAtAction(nameof(Get), new { id = created.Id }, created);
    }

    [Authorize(Policy = "OrderManager")]
    [HttpPut("{id:guid}/pay")]
    public async Task<ActionResult<OrderDto>> MarkPaid(
        Guid id,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken) =>
        Ok(await orderService.MarkPaidAsync(id, cancellationToken));
}

public sealed class CreateOrderRequest
{
    [Required, StringLength(120, MinimumLength = 2)]
    public string Customer { get; init; } = string.Empty;

    [Required, MinLength(1)]
    public IReadOnlyCollection<CreateOrderLineRequest> Lines { get; init; } = [];
}

public sealed class CreateOrderLineRequest
{
    [Required, StringLength(160, MinimumLength = 1)]
    public string Product { get; init; } = string.Empty;

    [Range(1, 10_000)]
    public int Quantity { get; init; }

    [Range(typeof(decimal), "0.01", "1000000000")]
    public decimal UnitPrice { get; init; }
}
src/OrderFlow.Infrastructure/OrderDbContext.cs
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using OrderFlow.Domain;

namespace OrderFlow.Infrastructure;

public sealed class OrderDbContext(DbContextOptions<OrderDbContext> options) : DbContext(options)
{
    public DbSet<Order> Orders => Set<Order>();

    protected override void OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder modelBuilder)
    {
        var order = modelBuilder.Entity<Order>();
        order.HasKey(item => item.Id);
        order.Property(item => item.Customer).HasMaxLength(120).IsRequired();
        order.Property(item => item.Status).HasConversion<string>().HasMaxLength(20);
        order.Ignore(item => item.Total);
        order.HasMany(item => item.Lines)
            .WithOne()
            .HasForeignKey("OrderId")
            .IsRequired()
            .OnDelete(DeleteBehavior.Cascade);
        order.Navigation(item => item.Lines)
            .UsePropertyAccessMode(PropertyAccessMode.Field);

        var line = modelBuilder.Entity<OrderLine>();
        line.HasKey(item => item.Id);
        line.Property(item => item.Product).HasMaxLength(160).IsRequired();
        line.Property(item => item.UnitPrice).HasPrecision(18, 2);
        line.Ignore(item => item.LineTotal);
    }
}

63. The Request Mental Model

○
Simple picture

A request is a parcel moving through checkpoints before reaching the correct handler, then travelling back as a response.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

Kestrel accepts HTTP, middleware handles cross-cutting concerns, routing selects an endpoint, model binding creates inputs, the endpoint calls application logic, and result execution writes status, headers and body.

Watch for this

The response travels back through middleware in reverse. Work after await next() is part of that return journey.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain The Request Mental Model, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

Memorise this picture:

MENTAL MODEL
Client
  ↓
HTTP request
  ↓
Kestrel
  ↓
Middleware pipeline
  ↓
Routing
  ↓
Controller / Endpoint
  ↓
Application service
  ↓
Repository / EF Core
  ↓
Database
  ↓
HTTP response

If you understand this flow, many ASP.NET questions become easier.

66. Middleware

○
Simple picture

Middleware is a chain of airport checkpoints: each component may inspect, change, stop or pass the request onward.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

A middleware delegate receives HttpContext and next. Code before await next() runs inbound; code after runs outbound. Order determines correctness for routing, auth, errors and caching.

Watch for this

If middleware does not call next, it short-circuits. Accidentally placing authentication after authorization or exception handling too late causes subtle failures.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain Middleware, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

Middleware is a component in the HTTP request pipeline.

Conceptually:

MENTAL MODEL
Request
  ↓
Exception handling / early logging
  ↓
HTTPS, static files and other early middleware as needed
  ↓
Routing selects the endpoint
  ↓
CORS
  ↓
Authentication
  ↓
Authorization
  ↓
The selected endpoint runs
  ↓
Response travels back

A middleware can:

  • inspect request;
  • modify request;
  • call next;
  • inspect/modify response;
  • stop the pipeline early.

Order matters. In the explicit mental model, routing must select an endpoint before authorization evaluates endpoint metadata; authentication comes before authorization. A minimal WebApplication can insert routing automatically when you do not call UseRouting, but you should still understand the logical order.

Examples:

  • exception handling;
  • HTTPS redirect;
  • CORS;
  • authentication;
  • authorization;
  • rate limiting;
  • logging.

Strong interview answer:

“

Middleware is an ordered pipeline of components that process HTTP requests and responses. Each middleware can perform work before/after the next component or short-circuit the pipeline.

69. HTTP Methods

○
Simple picture

HTTP verbs state the kind of intention: read, create, replace, change or remove.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

GET is safe and idempotent; PUT and DELETE are intended to be idempotent; POST is generally not; PATCH applies a partial change. Semantics guide retries, caching and client expectations.

Watch for this

Do not put state changes behind GET. A verb name in the URL does not repair incorrect HTTP semantics.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain HTTP Methods, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

You should know:

MENTAL MODEL
GET     → retrieve
POST    → create
PUT     → create or replace the selected resource representation (idempotent)
PATCH   → apply a partial change
DELETE  → delete

71. DTOs

○
Simple picture

A DTO is a travel-safe parcel shaped for the API boundary, not the database object itself.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

Request and response DTOs control fields, validation and versioning. Mapping prevents callers from over-posting internal properties and decouples the external contract from persistence.

Watch for this

Returning EF entities can leak navigation graphs, internal fields and tracking concerns. A DTO is not pointless duplication when it protects a boundary.

        get;
        set;
    }
}

DTOs help:

  • control API shape;
  • separate external contract from internal model;
  • validation;
  • security;
  • versioning/change management.

Authentication, authorization & development JWTs

Authentication asks “who are you?” Authorization asks “may this identity perform this action?” Think of authentication as showing a passport and authorization as checking whether the passport holder is on the staff list.

A JWT access token is three Base64URL parts: header, payload and signature. The payload contains claims such as user ID and roles. A signature helps the API detect tampering; it does not encrypt the payload. A real API validates signature, issuer, audience and expiry before trusting claims.

csharp
builder.Services
    .AddAuthentication(JwtBearerDefaults.AuthenticationScheme)
    .AddJwtBearer();

builder.Services.AddAuthorizationBuilder()
    .AddPolicy("OrderManager", policy => policy.RequireRole("OrderManager"));

app.UseAuthentication();
app.UseAuthorization();

The write endpoints use [Authorize(Policy = "OrderManager")]. Missing or invalid identity produces 401 Unauthorized; a valid identity without the required role produces 403 Forbidden. The integration tests prove both paths.

For local learning, let the .NET tooling issue a development token instead of writing password storage:

bash
dotnet user-jwts create --project src/OrderFlow.Api --role OrderManager

Copy the token into an Authorization: Bearer <token> header. In production, use a real identity provider, HTTPS, short-lived access tokens and server-side authorization on every protected operation. Never place secrets in a JWT payload or invent your own password hashing/token format.

○
Simple picture

   ↕

Instead of hand-writing every SQL query, you often express queries using LINQ and EF translates supported expressions to SQL.

82. IEnumerable<T> vs IQueryable<T>

○
Simple picture

IQueryable is a query plan still open to translation; IEnumerable is an item stream executed with .NET iteration rules.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

IQueryable<T> carries an expression tree and provider. Crossing into AsEnumerable or materialising normally moves subsequent operations to the client.

Watch for this

Exposing IQueryable across architectural boundaries leaks provider behaviour and lets callers create unbounded queries.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain IEnumerable<T> vs IQueryable<T>, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

High-yield interview question.

IEnumerable<T>

Represents enumeration of a sequence.

IQueryable<T>

Carries an expression that a query provider such as EF Core can translate.

Example:

csharp
IQueryable<Order> query =
    db.Orders
        .Where(o => o.Amount >= 100m);

Calling:

csharp
await query.ToListAsync();

causes execution/materialisation.

Important performance idea

Bad:

csharp
var everything =
    await db.Orders.ToListAsync();

var large =
    everything.Where(
        o => o.Amount >= 100m
    );

You loaded everything first.

Better:

csharp
var large =
    await db.Orders
        .Where(
            o => o.Amount >= 100m
        )
        .ToListAsync();

Let the database filter.

→ useful when updating entities

no tracking
→ good candidate for read-only queries

85. Migrations

○
Simple picture

A migration is version-controlled instructions that move the database schema from one known model shape to the next.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

EF compares the current model with its snapshot, generates migration operations and records applied migrations in the database. Review generated SQL for production.

Watch for this

Automatically applying migrations from every app instance at startup can race or exceed production permissions. Deployment strategy matters.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain Migrations, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

A migration records schema changes.

Conceptually:

MENTAL MODEL
change C# model
   ↓
create migration
   ↓
apply migration
   ↓
database schema updated

Common commands:

bash
dotnet ef migrations add InitialCreate

In this cumulative route, run the first migration checkpoint once and inspect what EF generated before applying it. CLI migration is appropriate for this local learning database. 86. N+1 Problem

○
Simple picture

N+1 means one query finds N parents, then an extra query is quietly sent for each parent.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

It commonly appears with lazy loading or queries inside loops. Projection, explicit eager loading or batching can make the required shape arrive in bounded queries.

Watch for this

Blindly including every navigation can create cartesian explosions. Measure SQL, row counts and payload shape.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain N+1 Problem, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

Imagine:

MENTAL MODEL
1 query → 100 orders
+
100 extra queries → items for each order

That is a classic N+1 shape.

Strong interview answer:

“

I would inspect the generated queries and reshape the query — often using projection or appropriate eager loading — so retrieving related data does not trigger one additional round trip per parent object.

The key problem is:

text
too many database round trips

88. Controller Should Not Become the Whole Application

○
Simple picture

A controller should be a receptionist, not the entire company: receive, delegate and translate the result.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

Thin controllers keep HTTP binding/status concerns at the edge while application services own use-case orchestration and domain objects own invariants.

‘Thin’ does not mean zero logic. Choosing a status code and mapping a request are legitimate controller responsibilities.

[HttpPost]
public async Task<ActionResult<OrderDto>> Create(CreateOrderRequest request, CancellationToken token)
{
    var command = new CreateOrderCommand(
        request.Customer,
        request.Lines.Select(line => new CreateOrderLineCommand(
            line.Product, line.Quantity, line.UnitPrice)).ToList());

    var created = await orderService.CreateAsync(command, token);
    return CreatedAtAction(nameof(Get), new { id = created.Id }, created);
}

tests/OrderFlow.UnitTests/OrderServiceTests.cs
using OrderFlow.Application;
using OrderFlow.Domain;

namespace OrderFlow.UnitTests;

public sealed class OrderServiceTests
{
    [Fact]
    public async Task Create_builds_and_saves_an_order()
    {
        var repository = new FakeOrderRepository();
        var service = new OrderService(repository, new SpyReceiptSender(), new FixedTimeProvider());
        var command = new CreateOrderCommand("Ada", [new("Keyboard", 2, 40m)]);

        var created = await service.CreateAsync(command, CancellationToken.None);

        Assert.Equal(80m, created.Total);
        Assert.Equal(DateTimeOffset.UnixEpoch, created.CreatedAtUtc);
        Assert.Equal(1, repository.SaveCount);
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task Paying_an_order_sends_one_receipt_even_when_retried()
    {
        var order = new Order("Ada", DateTimeOffset.UnixEpoch);
        order.AddLine("Keyboard", 1, 40m);
        var repository = new FakeOrderRepository(order);
        var receipt = new SpyReceiptSender();
        var service = new OrderService(repository, receipt, new FixedTimeProvider());

        await service.MarkPaidAsync(order.Id, CancellationToken.None);
        await service.MarkPaidAsync(order.Id, CancellationToken.None);

        Assert.Equal(1, receipt.SendCount);
        Assert.Equal(1, repository.SaveCount);
    }

    private sealed class FixedTimeProvider : TimeProvider
    {
        public override DateTimeOffset GetUtcNow() => DateTimeOffset.UnixEpoch;
    }

    private sealed class SpyReceiptSender : IReceiptSender
    {
        public int SendCount { get; private set; }
        public Task SendAsync(Order order, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
        {
            SendCount++;
            return Task.CompletedTask;
        }
    }

    private sealed class FakeOrderRepository(params Order[] seed) : IOrderRepository
    {
        private readonly List<Order> _orders = [.. seed];
        public int SaveCount { get; private set; }

        public Task AddAsync(Order order, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
        {
            _orders.Add(order);
            return Task.CompletedTask;
        }

        public Task<Order?> FindAsync(Guid id, CancellationToken cancellationToken) =>
            Task.FromResult(_orders.SingleOrDefault(order => order.Id == id));

        public Task<IReadOnlyList<Order>> ListAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken) =>
            Task.FromResult<IReadOnlyList<Order>>(_orders);

        public Task SaveChangesAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken)
        {
            SaveCount++;
            return Task.CompletedTask;
        }
    }
}

using System.Net;
using System.Net.Http.Json;

namespace OrderFlow.IntegrationTests;

public sealed class OrdersApiTests(TestWebApplicationFactory factory)
    : IClassFixture<TestWebApplicationFactory>
{
    private readonly HttpClient _client = factory.CreateClient();

    [Fact]
    public async Task Create_requires_authentication()
    {
        var response = await _client.PostAsJsonAsync("/api/orders", ValidOrder());

        Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.Unauthorized, response.StatusCode);
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task Create_requires_the_manager_role()
    {
        using var request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, "/api/orders")
        {
            Content = JsonContent.Create(ValidOrder())
        };
        request.Headers.Add("X-Test-User", "ada");

        var response = await _client.SendAsync(request, CancellationToken.None);

        Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.Forbidden, response.StatusCode);
    }

    [Fact]
    public async Task Manager_can_create_then_read_an_order()
    {
        using var create = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Post, "/api/orders")
        {
            Content = JsonContent.Create(ValidOrder())
        };
        create.Headers.Add("X-Test-User", "ada");
        create.Headers.Add("X-Test-Role", "OrderManager");

        var response = await _client.SendAsync(create, CancellationToken.None);
        var created = await response.Content.ReadFromJsonAsync<OrderResponse>(
            cancellationToken: CancellationToken.None);

        Assert.True(
            response.StatusCode == HttpStatusCode.Created,
            $"Expected 201 Created but received {(int)response.StatusCode}: " +
            await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync(CancellationToken.None));
        Assert.NotNull(created);
        Assert.Equal(80m, created.Total);

        var fetched = await _client.GetAsync(
            $"/api/orders/{created.Id}",
            CancellationToken.None);

        Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.OK, fetched.StatusCode);
    }

    private static object ValidOrder() => new
    {
        customer = "Ada",
        lines = new[] { new { product = "Keyboard", quantity = 2, unitPrice = 40m } }
    };

    private sealed record OrderResponse(Guid Id, decimal Total);
}

74. Why DI Exists

○
Simple picture

Dependency injection means a class asks for the tool it needs instead of secretly building the tool itself.

Go one layer deepertechnical truth · trap · recall check
Technical truth

The container resolves a constructor graph from registered abstractions and implementations. This makes dependencies visible and lets composition live at the application boundary.

Watch for this

DI is not primarily about mocks. Service location and injecting too many dependencies hide poor responsibility boundaries.

Prove you understand

Without looking: explain Why DI Exists, point to where it belongs in OrderFlow, then name one mistake or trade-off.

Bad tight coupling:

csharp
public class OrderService
{
    private readonly StripePaymentService
        _paymentService =
            new StripePaymentService();
}

OrderService decides exactly what implementation it gets.

Better:

csharp
public class OrderService
{
    private readonly IPaymentService
        _paymentService;

    public OrderService(
        IPaymentService paymentService)
    {
        _paymentService = paymentService;
    }
}

Now someone else provides the implementation.

That is constructor injection.
